text:
Filip Hronek's name is in the trade conversation now. The Canucks moved Max Sasson, and Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis wrote that Vancouver "appear to be open for business," with Hronek one of the names worth discussing. Whatever happens, he's carrying an enormous load in the meantime: 26:47 a night on the season and 28:19 over the last ten, with four games past 30 minutes.

The production is steady in one place. Eleven of his 17 points have come on the power play, and Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming there too. At five on five it's grim: Vancouver gets 36.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Hronek on the ice, 5.9 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey's note helps explain some of it, as his teammates rated in the bottom 6% by impact last season, which drags raw on-ice numbers down.

His one goal on 34 shots (2.9%) is below his usual range and should tick up. For anyone shopping a right-shot defenseman, the question is what he looks like with better partners and fewer minutes.
